title: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s
description: Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Gree
body: Young people would be offered a guaranteed two-year job within four months of leaving education or training, under a new proposal unveiled by the Green Party. Announcing the policy at the party's conference in Brighton, co-deputy leader Mothin Ali said there were a million "bored, desperate and lost" young people who were out of work, training or education.Under the proposed scheme, youngsters would be offered posts in the private sector, with the government paying half their salary.Ali said an initial pilot scheme - rolled out in areas with the fewest job openings for young people - would create 9,000 jobs, at an overall cost of £110m.The pilot would start in areas such as Rotherham, Ceredigion, Newcastle-under-Lyme, Broxtowe and South Staffordshire, with an ambition to roll it out nationwide.The party said that a person not in work, education or training would cost the state an estimated £240,000 in benefits over the course of their lifetime.It argued that its policy would reduce spending on welfare and boost tax receipts from employment. Employers would be exempt from paying National Insurance contributions, but would have to provide in-job training, the party says.The party is seeking to pitch the plan as more ambitious than the government's own scheme, which subsidises six-month job placements for benefit claimants who have been looking for work for 18 months. Ali also criticised ministers for previously suggesting youngsters refusing a role under that scheme could lose access to benefits, telling activists: "Threatening young people with cuts to Universal Credit if they don't accept short-term work placements - that's not a youth strategy."Speaking to BBC News after his speech, Ali said: "If we don't take action now, we're losing a generation of young people."The number of 16-24-year-olds who are not in employment, education or training has been rising since the Covid pandemic, with figures reaching almost one million. A long-awaited report into the problem by former Labour minister Alan Milburn is expected to be published this autumn. In her own speech to the conference, Ali's fellow co-deputy leader Rachel Millward said the Greens would immediately bring both Thames Water and South East Water back into public ownership.She argued this could be done without paying compensation to shareholders, pointing to water supply problems and a lack of new reservoirs.  Andy Burnham has promised to bring water under greater public control, but has stopped short of announcing plans to nationalise any water companies.Millward told the conference the prime minister was "making a mistake" and his "10-year plan of gentle threats and vague notions of control is not enough"."We need public ownership now, and we have all the tools we need to make it happen," she said. South East Water said it was "focused on delivering on our commitments by investing £1.9 billion into local infrastructure and resilience over the next five years."We support working closely with the communities we serve and are accountable to, so that we can provide the best possible service for customers".Thames Water has been approached for a response.

schema.headline: Greens would offer two-year jobs to unemployed under-24s

title: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution
description: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill
body: The head of prisons in the US state of Tennessee is resigning after the failed execution of death row inmate Christa Pike on Wednesday. Governor Bill Lee announced the change on Saturday, sharing the news in a joint statement with Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada.Strada said that his stepping down is "in the best interests" of the state, and called the ongoing investigation into the incident "entirely appropriate and necessary".Pike, who was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer, survived two injections and is now in critical condition at a Tennessee hospital as her lawyers seek to commute her sentence."Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," Lee said. Lee has ordered an independent review into Pike's attempted execution and he halted all executions in the state for the year.Attorney's for Pike called the resignation "justified" but said "it does nothing to help Christa now"."What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," Pike's legal team wrote in a statement. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."Pike is being treated at a hospital in Nashville, Tennessee, where doctors are attempting to clear the drugs used during the execution from her body, according to legal filings. She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance. While receiving the two doses, "she could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly throughout the procedure", her lawyers said.As of Thursday night, she was unconscious, intubated and on a ventilator. The state's Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".Authorities have not yet said whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have also not offered an explanation for what went wrong. Her lawyers filed an emergency motion on Friday to preserve "any and all evidence" related to her failed execution.Pike's attorneys previously warned that her medical history and anatomy - including thrombocytosis (a blood-clotting condition) and small veins - meant there was a risk she would experience "unnecessary" pain and suffering during a lethal injection.The attempted execution went ahead after multiple failed, last-minute legal challenges by Pike's lawyers.The US Supreme Court rejected two separate efforts to stop the lethal injection.Tennessee's governor also denied a clemency request from Pike, the only woman on the state's death row.Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer in 1995.She was sentenced to death the following year after a media frenzy around the killing in Knoxville, Tennessee.

schema.headline: Tennessee prison chief to resign after Christa Pike's failed execution

title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
description: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates pros
body: The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.A crash axe is usually kept ​in the cockpit in case of emergencies.The weapon used has been a key question for investigators, given the stringent security on such a sensitive route. Early reports from passengers on board had suggested it might have been a knife.The UAE attorney general told state media that investigations were ongoing to determine the full circumstances and motives of the incident.The co-pilot who launched the attack was an Omani national, according to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times have named him as Hamam al-Hammami. There has been no official confirmation of this.While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.He completed a three-year distance-learning course at Buckinghamshire New University in the UK and graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.Speaking to Fox News, Netanyahu said that after the attacker was subdued on the flight, he called out to the crew "Kill me, kill me!"The Israeli prime minister added: "So, it's clear that he was suicidal… It looks very likely that he was going to down the plane."He also said the attacker "underwent Islamist radical indoctrination".The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.He also said investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.Machchhar, who was stabbed in the attack, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.The pilot, who is from India, was in "good health and recovering well", the Indian embassy in the UAE said on Thursday."I am confident that the recovery will be there and I will become fit and healthy again," Machchhar said.About two and half hours after the plane took off from Dubai International Airport it begun to plunge sharply. The plane signalled a "general emergency" code, squawk 7700, before switching to squawk 7500, a code reporting "unlawful interference", or hijacking.In an interview with the BBC, one passenger described the moment he realised that something was wrong.Almog Itali said: "Suddenly the aeroplane started to, like a rollercoaster, to drop down [with] a massive G-force. It was falling down for 20 or 30 seconds, rapidly, and then balanced, and then started once again to fall down."People then began to rush to the cockpit, he said.Israeli President Isaac Herzog said on Thursday that the alarm was raised onboard by an Israeli woman, Tali Manes, who heard a commotion coming from the cockpit. Her husband, Zvika, along with three other men - Yaniv Hayun, Dr Shota Musayev and Asaf Rajuan - entered the cockpit after Capt Machchhar managed to open the door despite his injuries. Hayun said, in a video released by the prime minister's office, that the attacker was "trying to destroy the instruments in order to disable the plane".Hayun then described putting the attacker in a chokehold and pulling him outside the cockpit before other passengers helped to pin him down.He added that he "pulled the controls" of the plane. "The plane started to level out, a bit more, and then [another] pilot told me he was taking control from there," he said.In an interview with CNN on Wednesday evening, Netanyahu said the stabbed pilot, passengers and second crew had "managed to prevent a 9/11 disaster".

schema.headline: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says

title: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed
description: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on
body: A UK-Iranian dual national arrested on suspicion of preparation of terrorist acts in connection with an incident at RAF Fairford has been released on bail.The 25-year-old man was arrested in the London borough of Westminster on Thursday. Searches of two properties in the same area have now finished. A major incident was declared and dozens of homes were evacuated after police were alerted to three "suspicious vehicles" near the airbase in Gloucestershire last weekend.Five other men in their twenties were arrested and were subsequently released on police bail. All five were UK nationals from London.The investigation into the circumstances surrounding the events are continuing, police said.Last weekend, the five men aged between 23 and 25 were arrested in the early hours of the morning after vehicles were reported to be travelling towards the base operated by the US Air Force (USAF), sparking a major security incident.The BBC understands that one of the men had dialled 999 himself, about an hour before a local farmer alerted police to a "large group" of masked men near the vehicles.They were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later on suspicion of preparing a terrorist act, before being released on bail on Monday in what police called an "investigative decision" that was "grounded in experience and strategy".Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting that afternoon in response. He later said there were "strong indications" that Iran had played a part in the incident, but did not provide any more details.Tehran has strongly denied any involvement. The Iranian embassy in London said on Monday that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.RAF Fairford has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".Late on Monday, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a TV show that it was clear a "foreign actor" had been involved in events over the weekend.Without providing evidence or giving further details, he told Fox News network's "Hannity" programme: "What happened, what almost happened, what could have happened in the UK over the weekend is a very serious situation. It's one that clearly involves the hands of a foreign actor."Speaking earlier at the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump said he would not have let the five men arrested out on bail, and that he was "surprised" they had been released."We know everything about them, we would not have released them," he said, adding that the UK had worked with the US "very closely" on this.

schema.headline: UK-Iranian dual national arrested over RAF Fairford investigation bailed

title: Republic of Ireland v Israel: News conference ends amid accusations
description: The Republic of Ireland's news conference before their second match against Israel ended abruptly as head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson fielded questions
body: The Republic of Ireland's news conference before their second match against Israel ended abruptly as head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson fielded questions from Israeli journalists.One reporter tried to ask Hallgrimsson for his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday when a co-pilot attacked a pilot on a flight travelling from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers overpowered the attacker and successfully took control of the plane.The Republic of Ireland manager was also asked by another journalist, who refused to give up the microphone, about alleged racism by Irish players during last Sunday's 3-0 win over Israel in Hungary.The news conference was brought to a close at that point by Football Association of Ireland (FAI) communications manager Kieran Crowley, who said those allegations were "completely untrue" as the mood soured.Allegations of racism by Irish players follow on from the FAI announcing it is investigating reports of racist abuse directed towards Republic of Ireland striker Adam Idah by Israel fans during the first match in Debrecen, which Hallgrimsson's team won 3-0.At Israel's news conference later in the day, the team's media officer stepped in to confirm the Israel FA has not lodged a complaint with Uefa but "will think about that after the match tomorrow"."Our players told us there was trash talk between the Irish players and them that was not like normal or like any other match," the media officer said.Head coach Ran Ben-Shimon did not want to address such matters, insisting "a good result tomorrow is my only focus".Before the Irish news conference was cut short, Hallgrimsson said similar as he stressed he would not "get involved in that as others will process that"."It is a game with a lot of emotions attached," Hallgrimsson said."I haven't read anything and it's not something I want to get involved with. It goes to a process, both in our department and with Uefa."Something was reported by both teams, so I just hope we can focus on football and football will be the winner after this."I have not gone into details looking at this as I have enough to think about."This has been a challenging international window for the Republic of Ireland, with the Israel fixtures dominating discourse in Irish football.Since the teams were drawn together in February, a 'Stop The Game' campaign was launched by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine, which called for a boycott of the fixtures in protest against the ongoing Israel-Gaza war.Before last week's 'home' game for Israel in Hungary, Republic of Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the fixtures, saying "it would be wrong to participate", while a vote by players to play the games passed by a "significant majority", according to FAI chief executive David Courell.The players wore black armbands during the game "in recognition of all lives lost in the [Gaza] conflict".The Republic of Ireland then played Austria in Dublin on Thursday, when protests resulted in tennis balls being thrown on to the pitch and a protester briefly interrupting the game when he ran on to the turf, waving a Palestine flag.Hallgrimsson said under the circumstances, it will be a "a big win for this group and the association if we go through undamaged".They have four points from three games so far, having beaten Israel and drawn 2-2 with Austria. They lost 1-0 to Kosovo in the campaign opener."The most pleasing thing for me is to see the togetherness and how they stand up for each other," Hallgrimsson said."Whatever they have done, they have done it with respect to the situation, to each other and after this, this bond of brothers will be stronger than ever. All the obstacles this group will face in the future will be lesser than it is."When we look back, this camp will be a moment we grew the most and stepped up as leaders, supported each other and stuck together. The power of togetherness is stronger than individuals."The Republic of Ireland boss revealed the team have taken part in a group prayer before leaving the dressing room for recent games, which he said was "just to cool our heads before we go on to the pitch".He said that has been led by midfielder Conor Coventry whom he joked is now known within the squad as "Brother Coventry".The Icelander said Dara O'Shea - the team's captain in place of the injured Nathan Collins - was not with the squad, as his wife was due to give birth. He may arrive back in Backa Topola prior to Sunday's 19:45 BST kick-off.

schema.headline: Republic of Ireland v Israel: News conference ends amid accusations

title: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final
description: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challengeImage source, Richard Sellers/PAImage caption, Kevin Sinfield carried the Super League Grand Final tro
body: Sinfield completes final ultramarathon challengeImage source, Richard Sellers/PAImage caption, Kevin Sinfield carried the Super League Grand Final trophy into Old Trafford after completing the challengeByGrace WoodYorkshireSir Kevin Sinfield has completed his latest endurance challenge raising money for motor neurone disease (MND) causes in memory of his friend and teammate Rob Burrow, who died in 2024.Sinfield completed seven ultramarathons in seven days, crossing the finish line at Old Trafford Stadium in Manchester ahead of the Super League Grand Final.The fundraiser and his team have raised more than £13m for the MND community since his first annual challenge in 2020.Speaking to the crowd, Sinfield said: "The rugby league community has got right behind the MND community and Rob would be so proud to see how you've supported and cared, and showed your love for a community that really needs us."Sinfield began his final ultramarathon challenge in Hull on September 27 and visited all 12 Super League clubs along the way.The 7 in 7: The Grand Finale week ended at Old Trafford earlier where he brought out the trophy ahead of the game between Warrington Wolves and Wakefield Trinity.Image source, PA MediaImage caption, Prince William and Catherine made an unexpected appearance in Wakefield on Tuesday to meet Sir KevinAlong the way he was surprised by royals, including The Prince and Princess of Wales and the Princess Royal, as well as famous names from the sporting world such as former England football manager Sir Gareth Southgate and Leeds boxer Josh Warrington.Each day was split into 7km, hour-long blocks with an additional extra mile for members of the MND community to join.Funds raised by the challenge will go towards the work of the MND Association, Leeds Hospitals Charity, My Name5 Doddie Foundation, Darby Rimmer Foundation, MND Scotland and the Irish MND Association.Image source, Mike Egerton/PAImage caption, Sinfield arrived at Old Trafford at about 17:00 BSTSinfield, 45, who played his entire professional career with Leeds Rhinos, is one of the most successful players in Super League history.He and Burrow met at the Leeds Rhinos academy aged 14 and 12. They went on to win seven titles together with Leeds Rhinos.Burrow's wife, Lindsey Burrow, told BBC Radio 4's PM that her late husband "would have been incredibly proud" of his friend."It's bittersweet that Rob's not here today to see Kevin finish his final challenge but Rob will be with us in spirit and it's just testimony to Kevin that he's so humbled to do this not just for Rob but for the whole MND community," Lindsey said."It's just incredible. I am in complete awe of the efforts of Kevin and his team over the last seven days, and not just over the last seven days but over the last seven years," she added.Sinfield's son, Jack Sinfield, lined up in the Wakefield side seeking to clinch their first top-flight title since 1968.Get in touchYour Voice

schema.headline: Sir Kevin Sinfield completes epic challenge ahead of Grand Final

title: Celebrity Traitors: First victim claimed as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin
description: Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a T
body: Spoiler warning: This article reveals details from the second episode of The Celebrity Traitors, series two.A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment."It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day."But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."The episode drew in a peak audience of 8.6 million viewers, just short of the debut episode with an average of 8.9 million viewers.The morning following Rajan's banishment, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.The players made their way to the mission, which had the usual slightly convoluted rules that took Winkleman quite a while to explain.In a nutshell, the celebrities were to be buried alive in pairs, with only one duo left above ground.Ross Kemp was pre-selected by the traitors to be protected from burial along with his grave partner Romesh Ranganathan, who did a delightful dance when he found out he wouldn't be going underground.Kemp and Ranganathan then had the opportunity to dig up some gold graves which would add to the prize pot, or alternatively dig up and free their fellow players.They opted for the latter, which resulted in some other players struggling, external to get the soil off their faces. In the end, all the celebrities were released, with the exception of Fry and Hall.The pair were freed early after Hall shouted the emergency word "Haggis!" – effectively a Scottish version of "I'm a celebrity get me out of here!" - because she was visibly uncomfortable being buried alive.It might have led to an early release, but it ultimately guaranteed that either she or Fry will be murdered next, unless the traitors recruit again."Just you and me up for murder," Fry told Hall afterwards. "You'd better not be a traitor or I'm really screwed!"In a flashback shown to viewers, Acaster explained the decision to protect Kemp from burial, telling his fellow traitors: "I think if we give it to Ross, he'll overthink it, and behave in a way that would draw suspicion."Very clever. "You're a wonderful traitor," observed Grant. (Certainly better than him.)As discussions got going, it took a surprisingly long time for Grant's name to come up, as the other players debated other suspects such as Julie Hesmondhalgh.The actress aroused suspicion because she was the first celebrity this year to receive a shield. The group seemed to have overlooked she only got that - in the opening minutes of the first show - after the other contestants voted her the most trustworthy.But as discussion turned to Grant, Hesmondhalgh put forward one of the most convincing cases of the night."You came into the bar, and said you were a traitor," she told him. "It was a bold move. It was chaotic and we love you for your chaos."I think we are at risk of being the most idiotic group of faithfuls in the world, if we go for someone else tonight based on nothing at all, when somebody has come into the room and said 'I am a traitor'. There's no reason to say it unless you are."Miranda Hart agreed that "the joy when he took off his blindfold" when Winkleman first selected the traitors made Grant look suspicious.

schema.headline: Celebrity Traitors: First victim claimed as Richard E Grant tries to save his skin

title: England player ratings v Croatia: Who was the best player on the pitch?
description: Jordan Pickford: A really good decision and save when he raced out and won the ball at the feet of Ivan Perisic early on. Not tested but was lucky to
body: Jordan Pickford: A really good decision and save when he raced out and won the ball at the feet of Ivan Perisic early on. Not tested but was lucky to not concede with Mateo Kovacic's incredible miss. 6Jarell Quansah: Surprisingly chosen at right-back over Trent Alexander-Arnold but the Bayer Leverkusen defender does exactly what manager Thomas Tuchel wants. A powerful runner, a good defender and his ability on the ball is underrated - he showed it with a quality assist for Gordon. 8Ezri Konsa: Not loads of defending for Konsa to do as England pinned Croatia back but it was a calm assured performance from the defender. 7Marc Guehi: The centre-back had to take up some risky positions as England pressed man for man all over the pitch. 7Lewis Hall: The Newcastle left-back looks a great addition to the England back four. Hall offers pace going forward and also underlapped, going into midfield to recieve the ball. 7 Elliot Anderson: Anderson has been excellent throughout this international break and produced another mature performance. The Manchester City midfielder is a crucial part of the midfield and set up Kane for England's fifth. 8Alex Scott: The Bournemouth midfielder was given his first England start and put in a really confident performance. Scott always looked to get on the ball and did not just try to keep it safe as England dominated. 7Jude Bellingham: The best player on the pitch. Bellingham produced a lovely pass to thread Kane through for the first goal, scored England's second and assisted Saka for England's fourth. A truly world-class player and his quality was too much for Croatia throughout the game. 9Bukayo Saka: The winger scored twice and looks to be building a good partnership with Quansah on England's right-hand side. Saka could have had a hat-trick but missed a big chance in the second half. 8Anthony Gordon: Playing with a huge amount of confidence and continues to show that he has gone to another level in recent months. Assisted Bellingham and scored for the fourth England game in a row. 9Harry Kane: Just an elite finisher and his goal put England firmly in control. The captain looked full of energy, pressed from the front and showed his passing range as he enjoyed having Gordon and Bellingham supplying him. Scored England's fifth goal too. 9

schema.headline: England player ratings v Croatia: Who was the best player on the pitch?

title: Why electric cars might be making some passengers feel sick
description: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be whyImage source, Getty Images/Halfpoint ImagesByGrace DeanLola Baird has jus
body: EV drivers love their cars, but some passengers feel sick - this could be whyImage source, Getty Images/Halfpoint ImagesByGrace DeanLola Baird has just asked her boyfriend to pull over. Forty minutes into a journey and she's feeling "overwhelmed" by nausea - and can't stop herself throwing up on the ground next to his car.Lola, 24, from north London, had never experienced motion sickness until her boyfriend bought an electric vehicle (EV) two years ago. Ever since, she's been feeling "very nauseous" when he takes her on long car journeys.It's become so severe she's even asked him to change his car.Lola isn't alone. Other people told BBC News that they or their children notice feeling more car sick when sitting as a passenger in an electric vehicle. But at the same time, many EV drivers say it's not been a concern.So what could explain these reports of motion sickness?Dr Irene Di Giulio, senior lecturer in anatomy and biomechanics at King's College London whose research includes motion sickness, says research so far suggests some people experience more severe motion sickness in electric vehicles than in non-electric vehicles.It's something Dr Nicholas Hac, a neurologist at Northwestern Medicine in Chicago who specialises in dizziness and vertigo, has also heard from some of his patients. "They just notice that they're much more likely or prone to be motion sick" in electric vehicles, he says."I've heard about it many, many, many times," he adds, saying about two patients a month specifically reference feeling motion sick in electric vehicles.Image source, Lola BairdImage caption, Lola Baird noticed that she felt sick in electric vehicle taxis as well as her boyfriend's car. "I started to put two and two together," she saysBut research into any possible link is still in its early stages, and some academics say there isn't sufficient evidence to say anything definitive.Dr Bill Yates, who has researched motion sickness at the University of Pittsburgh, says the body of research is "pretty sketchy at this point"."There's some anecdotal information, but not a lot of really serious, extensive studies done yet," he says.'Wonderful to drive... but my daughter gets unwell'When Mark Quigg was looking at options for a new car last year, an electric vehicle seemed like the best choice because of the lower running costs. Mark, 45, from Lincolnshire, says his shiny new electric vehicle has been "wonderful" to drive - but he quickly noticed that his nine-year-old daughter's motion sickness got much worse in it.She only used to get motion sick on their 600-mile drives to France during the school holidays, but now he says even the 30-minute trip to the nearest city makes his daughter feel unwell.On one recent journey, he says his daughter even threw up, which had never happened before.Image source, Mark QuiggImage caption, Mark Quigg says electric cars are a "lovely driving experience for me, personally, because they are a lot quieter"Motion sickness doesn't affect all EV passengers - many owners got in touch with BBC News to say they and their relatives don't get sick in electric vehicles. Others said they felt less sick in EVs compared with traditional combustion engine cars.Vicky Edmonds, the CEO of EVA England, an association for electric vehicle drivers, says motion sickness isn't a concern among her members. "This has never come up as an issue," she says.But Chinese electric vehicle maker XPeng, which has showrooms across the UK, has previously publicly addressed the issue, external, telling people who've noticed a link between electric vehicles and travel sickness that "it's a fair question, and it's not your imagination". It's caused by "side effects of how electric cars are engineered," it adds.What could cause it?Motion sickness is caused by "a mismatch in sensory cues," Hac says. Our bodies rely on three main sensory inputs to show that we're moving, which come from what we see, what our inner ear's balance system perceives, and what fibres in our body sense, he says. When one of these is in conflict with the others - like if you're looking at your phone so you don't see visual signs of movement out of the window - that can cause motion sickness.Research suggests several reasons why it may be more severe in electric vehicles.Humans have adapted to associate sound with movement in vehicles, experts explain. Because electric vehicles don't have the auditory cues and vibrations from the engine that we're used to, which indicate when the car is accelerating, this could trigger motion sickness, Di Giulio says.Another reason is regenerative braking, the process whereby when drivers release the accelerator, the motor starts acting as a generator. This creates resistance that slows the car down and also produces electricity that can be stored in the battery. The accelerator needs to be released gently, or it can lead to harsh deceleration."It forces the person to perhaps feel like they're rocking back and forth for that brief moment when the speed of the car suddenly changes," says Hac.This is something Carolyn Le, 24, from California, has noticed. She gets "horrendous" motion sickness when her friend drives her in his electric vehicle in busy cities, she says. The regenerative braking means it "constantly feels like the car is stopping all the time".Image source, Carolyn LeImage caption, "It's actually horrendous," says Carolyn Le, who blames regenerative braking for her motion sicknessElectric vehicles can also accelerate and decelerate much more quickly than conventional combustion cars, which Di Giulio says can cause motion sickness.Edmonds, of EVA England, says developments in electric vehicle design have made them better at moderating the acceleration so they don't gain speed as rapidly.She adds that the association thinks motion sickness in an electric vehicle is caused by "other factors" like the motorist's driving style rather than the vehicle itself. Some features of electric cars may feel unfamiliar to drivers at first, adds Mike Hawes, head of the Society of Motor Manufacturers.He says EVs can offer a different driving experience. "However, drivers typically adjust quickly to these characteristics, and many models also allow regenerative braking to be tailored to individual preferences."Some people are also just more prone to motion sickness, and genetics have the biggest influence on this, according to Hac, and experts say women and children are more susceptible.Motion sickness typically peaks between the ages of eight and 10, after which it decreases through more exposure, says Prof John Golding, who has researched the subject at the University of Westminster, the Royal Navy and the RAF.Hold your head still and open the windowAs their popularity increases, avoiding electric vehicles can be a challenge - the number of new zero-emission cars registered in the UK rose by 40.5% in April to June 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, latest Department for Transport figures show. , externalAt the end of June 2026, 5.8% of all licensed cars on UK roads were zero-emission vehicles, the data shows. The sale of new purely petrol or diesel cars is set to be banned from 2030.Lucinda Harrison, 24, from London says she often books taxis that turn out to be electric vehicles, and has to endure the trip feeling nauseous, sweaty and clammy.The thought of travelling in an EV fills her with dread, she says. Even just a five-minute lift from a colleague to a Tube station recently was enough to make her feel "horrific".Academics say there are several steps passengers can take to reduce feelings of motion sickness.Look out of the front window and don't look at your phone or read a bookSit in the front passenger seat rather than in the back, if possible. If you do have to sit in the back, opt for the middle seat so you can still see out the front windowKeep your head still by holding it against the headrestRecline your seatRegulate your breathingOpen the window to let in fresh airTake travel sickness tablets if needed, though these can cause drowsinessBefore a long journey, make sure you're hydrated, have slept well and have eaten non-greasy foodExperts also say we can become desensitised to motion sickness through prolonged exposure. The more journeys you take in electric vehicles, the less likely you are to become motion sick as your body adjusts, Golding says.Image source, Getty Images/Cyndi MonaghanImage caption, Looking out the window can ease motion sickness, which children and women may be more prone to experiencing as passengersThere are also things carmakers can do to alleviate motion sickness in electric vehicles, says Prof Cyriel Diels, professor of mobility design at the Royal College of Art. These include having software that smooths out rapid acceleration, adding sound systems and subtle seat vibrations to signal to passengers that the car is moving, and offering adaptive regenerative braking that reduces sudden deceleration.In some EVs, regenerative braking can also often be turned off.Matt Adams from BEAMA, which represents UK manufacturers of electric vehicle charge points, says he's confident that "if future research identifies the reason for car sickness that vehicle manufacturers can respond and improve accordingly".But for Lola, she just wants her boyfriend to trade in his car. She says that day can't come soon enough.Get in touchAre you an EV driver or have been a passenger in an EV? Have you experienced nausea due to motion sickness? Tell us your story.

schema.headline: Why electric cars might be making some passengers feel sick

title: New life for dog rescued with 83 others from Doncaster house
description: The owner recalled Katy's first few days at her new home, where she initially refused to venture onto the grass. "She stayed on the patio because I do
body: The owner recalled Katy's first few days at her new home, where she initially refused to venture onto the grass. "She stayed on the patio because I don't think she knew what the grass was," Wendy added."She did everything she needed to on there and then the second day, she was romping around the grass chasing the butterflies."It didn't take her long to figure out that she was safe and she was home."When Katy and the other dogs were found, officers reported the kitchen being covered in dirt and faeces "from floor to ceiling". More than 30 dogs were crowded together on the stairs, while others climbed on the kitchen sides or cowered in corners.Although the family responsible for the animals was inside the property, police had to force entry.Faye Gibbons, from the RSPCA, remembered when Katy had been brought into their care."We could see that she was traumatised," she said."The team were very shocked at just how difficult she was finding her new surroundings."When she first arrived, her coat was stained in urine, with faeces."It was just a harrowing sight and probably one of the hardest cases our team have worked on."On Tuesday, children's social worker David Parkes was found guilty of failing to ensure the welfare of the animals, which were kept at the home he shared with his family.He had denied animal welfare offences, claiming his wife, Delphine, and son, Sam, were primarily responsible for the dogs' care due to his heavy workload.However, the 61-year-old was found guilty following a two-day trial at Barnsley Magistrates' Court.Delphine Parkes, 60, and Sam Parkes, 28, pleaded guilty to the same offences at a hearing earlier this year. All three will be sentenced on 9 December.An RSPCA spokesperson said one of the dogs later had to be put to sleep due to ongoing health issues, but all of the others had been rehomed.Faye Gibbons agreed Katy was a very lucky dog. "Just looking at her here, she's landed on a paws, let's say," she added.

schema.headline: New life for dog rescued with 83 others from Doncaster house

title: Man shot dead in East Acton as people gather for memorial service
description: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including childre
body: A murder investigation has been launched after a 40-year-old man was shot dead in a "senseless act of violence" as up to 50 people – including children – gathered for a memorial service in west London.The Met Police said it was called to the scene at 19:47 GMT on Friday after multiple shots had been heard by members of the public at the junction of Braybrook Street and Erconwald Street in East Acton.Officers attended alongside the London Ambulance Service but the man was pronounced dead at the scene, despite the efforts of medics.No arrests have been made and a police cordon remains in place in Braybrook Street. Police are appealing for witnesses to come forward.The victim's family have been informed and are being supported by specialist officers.A post-mortem examination is scheduled to establish the cause of death, but the victim is believed to have sustained a gunshot wound, the force said.Det Ch Insp Brian Howie, who is leading the investigation, said: "Our thoughts are with the family and friends of a man whose life was taken in a senseless act of violence."We understand a large number of people had gathered for a memorial service and what should have been a time to come together in remembrance has instead left a family devastated."We believe between 40 and 50 people, including children, were present when this incident occurred. Someone knows what happened and we need them to come forward."He has asked anyone who was around Erconwald Street, Braybrook Street, the surrounding roads or Wormwood Scrubs playground between 18:00 and 20:00, to "please think carefully about what you saw". He added: "Did you see anyone carrying or concealing weapons, people on bicycles acting suspiciously, or vehicles being driven at speed?"We also want to hear from anyone with photographs, video, dashcam, doorbell or mobile phone footage or who has seen anything relevant on social media."However insignificant it may seem, the smallest piece of information could prove crucial in helping us establish what happened and identify those responsible."Listen to the best of BBC Radio London on Sounds and follow BBC London on Facebook,, external X,, external and Instagram., external Send your story ideas to hello.bbclondon@bbc.co.uk

title: The Prem: Gloucester 48-0 Harlequins: Cherry and Whites thrash pointless Quins
description: The PremGloucester (24) 48Tries: Loader, Morgan, Trenholm, C. Atkinson, S. Atkinson, Englefield, Joseph, Barton Cons: Barton 4Harlequins (0) 0Gloucest
body: The PremGloucester (24) 48Tries: Loader, Morgan, Trenholm, C. Atkinson, S. Atkinson, Englefield, Joseph, Barton Cons: Barton 4Harlequins (0) 0Gloucester thrashed a limp Harlequins at Kingsholm to go to the top of the early Prem standings.The Cherry and Whites ran in eight tries to make it two wins from two in the league and three on the bounce in all competitions.Gloucester, who named three new signings in their starting line-up including Wales internationals Jac Morgan and Dewi Lake, completely outplayed their opponents in all facets of the match.Visitors Quins, who handed a debut to England full-back George Furbank, struggled to get a handle on the game from the outset and remain bottom of the table without any points after failing to get on the scoreboard.A progressive move down the right gave Gloucester fly-half Charlie Atkinson – three days after he signed a new deal committing his long-term future with the club - the opportunity to find Ben Loader free on the left with a pinpoint kick, and the winger dotted down to open the scoring.Harlequins, in their desperation to keep Gloucester out on their own try line, lost Will Evans to the sin bin and mere seconds later Wales flanker Morgan barged over in the left corner to extend Gloucester's lead.On the stroke of half hour, Morgan's strong carry allowed Will Trenholm to force over Gloucester's third try from close range before George Barton slotted the conversio superbly from touch.A spectacular 50:22 from scrum-half Caolan Englefield then put Gloucester in another great position and Charlie Atkinson broke a tackle to go over next to the sticks, as Barton kicked an easy extra two to give the hosts a 24-point advantage at half-time.The interval did not change the momentum as two short passes saw Seb Atkinson race to the line and power over Gloucester's fifth of the evening and Quins' day was perhaps summed up best when Connor Slevin's poor restart failed to go 10 metres.Gloucester ruthlessly made their visitors pay once more as with their next attack Will Joseph's outstanding run and offload allowed Englefield to dive over.Joseph then grabbed the try his own performance deserved, diving in to the right of the posts to claim Gloucester's seventh try and third inside 12 minutes after half-time.Another kick to the corner from Charlie Atkinson found Barton who juggled successfully and managed to extend over for Gloucester's eighth.Joseph thought he had scored his second with the final act of the match to take Gloucester past 50 points, but his try was chalked off for a knock-on in the build up.Gloucester: Barton; Thorley, Joseph, S. Atkinson, Loader; C. Atkinson, Englefield; Rapava-Ruskin, Lake (capt), Fasogbon, Kleyn, Clark, Thomas, Morgan, Trenholm.Replacements: Innard, Bleuler, C. Knight, Clement, Ludlow, Robson, W. Knight, Denny.Harlequins: Furbank; Anderson, Beard, Bradley, Murley (capt); Slevin, Porter; Hobson, Walker, Delgado, Dun, Browne, Kenningham, Evans, Carr.Sin-bin: Evans (17 mins)Replacements: Riley, Wenger, Kerrod, Petti, Cunningham-South, Friday, Lang, Green.Referee: Sara Cox.

title: You need £17,000 for a first home - here's how to save it
description: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the mo
body: Figure caption, How much is in your savings account?ByCost of living correspondentIf buying your own home is the finishing line, then saving up the money to get there is a marathon.The "Your First Home" scheme, announced on Saturday, aims to help first-time buyers in England get on the housing ladder with a small deposit.Currently a 5% deposit on the average UK house price of £272,000 plus moving costs and legal fees - will set you back about £16,850, according to financial information service Moneyfacts.That's daunting, but here are four ways that experts say you can at least make a start on saving for a deposit.1. Make saving like a billDepositing an amount you can afford into a regular savers account the day after you are paid is a good way to start, suggests Anna Bowes, savings expert at financial advisers The Private Office."It becomes like another bill, but one that you can benefit from in the future," she says.The type of account that's suitable depends on your circumstances.Some of the ones that pay the highest interest  are only accessible if you hold a current account with the provider, she says.Other considerations are whether you can lock the money away for longer, to receive a better savings rate.If you don't have a buffer of other savings, then experts say an easy access account gives you the chance to dip into the money to pay an unexpected bill.2. You could get £1,000 a year You can save up to £4,000 a year in a Lifetime Individual Savings Account (LISA) and the government guarantees a 25% bonus. So, if you put the full amount in then the government will add £1,000 a year. But there is a catch, that has left some people out of pocket. Money saved in a LISA can only be used to buy a first home up to the value of £450,000 - a threshold that has not changed since 2017. The only other time you can withdraw the money is after the age of 60 or in the exceptional case that you are terminally ill with less than 12 months to live.Withdrawal under any other circumstances means you get hit with a penalty - so you could get back less than you put in.Ministers are planning to replace the LISA with a new First Time Buyer ISA, but there are no clear details yet about how it will work.3. Start earlyThe earlier you start saving the more you can build up thanks to the magic of compound interest. In short, interest is added on a larger and larger pot as time goes by.Bowes says that saving £50 a month from the age of 20 would give you about £41,000 in 30 years' time when you hit 50, assuming interest of 5% is paid a year.Start 10 years later, and you'd need to save more than double - £101 a month - to have the same amount at the age of 50.Investing in stocks and shares is another option, but the value of investments can go down as well as up.4. Save lessAn increasing number of lenders are offering mortgage deals with little or no deposit required.David Hollingworth, from L&C, points to mortgages that have deposits starting from £5,000 and allow people to borrow up to 98% or 99% of the property purchase price.They might not always be the best option, and not everyone will be eligible.And, of course, some first-time buyers turn to their parents for help. Again that's not available to all, but a survey by the Nationwide Building Society suggests that more than half of parents who charge their adult children rent are putting some or all of the money towards helping their child save to buy their own home.Get in touchAre you trying to get on to the property ladder? Share your experience. Get our flagship newsletter with all the headlines you need to start the day. Sign up here.

title: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
description: A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukr
body: A Russian strike has hit a second major bridge in Kyiv, Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko has said, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital.The attack on Saturday morning injured two people, and damaged the road surface and overhead trolleybus wires on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, Klitschko said, causing traffic jams.It comes after the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times by Russian drones this week, with Klitschko warning that "the enemy is tearing Kyiv apart".Russia said its drones had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops and military cargo. Moscow again urged foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv. The two Kyiv bridges across the Dnipro River link the western and eastern parts of the capital and had not been hit before Thursday.The Russian strikes have severed road, rail and trolleybus links across the wide river. The ongoing drone threat means restrictions on other routes, bringing traffic jams to the city's roads for a second day - though Friday's gridlock has not been repeated to the same level.Many of the city's residents - which number about three million - rely on the metro to travel across the city every day. The fear is this new Russian tactic will result in sustained attacks which could effectively cut the city in two.Writing on Telegram on Saturday morning, Klitschko said "emergency services are on their way" after the Pivnichnyi Bridge was hit."Traffic on the bridge from the left to the right bank is currently blocked," he added.Earlier attacks on the Pivdennyi Bridge prompted Kyiv's defence council to hold a crisis meeting on Friday. Klitschko warned afterwards that the city was now in a "very dramatic situation" as Moscow was battering its "critical infrastructure, logistics, housing" and other key facilities.Experts say Russian drones are unlikely to bring down the bridges - but repeated attacks will force their closure and risk weakening their structure, making them unusable. More powerful weapons could collapse the bridges, some of which are reported to be in poor condition after years carrying heavier traffic than they were designed for.It was reported that Ukrainian lawmakers discussed the state of Kyiv's bridges in a recent meeting, setting out contingency plans to use ferries or temporary pontoon bridges to keep the city connected in the event of any bridges being destroyed.Russian President Vladimir Putin has said Russia is acting in response to Ukraine's strikes on Russian energy facilities, despite the fact that it was Moscow that had first launched such attacks.After the Pivdennyi Bridge was attacked, passengers described how dust from a blast wave entered their carriage through the ventilation system.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Putin had decided that there were "no rules now" when attacking Ukraine. In an interview with the Financial Times, he said: "The Russians have failed to occupy us. So now they are carrying out massive attacks and mass killings."He added: "They want to destroy our bridges... our data centres, the internet, mobile networks, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, universities - everything. They want people to flee their cities."Putin on Thursday insisted that Russia's attacks on Ukrainian economic targets were a direct response to Ukraine's strikes on Russia's oil refineries and its ships in the Black Sea."Now from every direction we're receiving calls 'let's stop'. But they started it," Putin said after a wide-ranging speech at the Valdai foreign policy forum.The Kremlin leader admitted Kyiv had "got some results" from its refinery attacks and Russia had lost about 1% of its GDP. Ukraine maintains it began attacking Russian oil infrastructure because it helps the Kremlin finance the war.Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure, ramping up attacks every winter since Putin launched a full-scale invasion in February 2022.

schema.headline: Russia hits second major bridge in Ukraine's capital Kyiv
